title: Reading plans (orders from named sources)
rightsNote: M’Cheyne’s calendar (1842) is public domain, transcribed from Haslam’s PDF with two recorded corrections. The chronological arrangement is Wellspring’s own (CC0). The “order written” list uses dates tabled in Wikipedia’s “Dating the Bible” as facts. The Septuagint order is Rahlfs’s as printed in NETS; the 1611 order is Barker’s contents table. No plan carries devotional text.
citation: Wellspring reading plans; each plan names its source on its card.

plans.title: M’Cheyne’s calendar
plans.source: Robert Murray M’Cheyne, Daily Bread: being a calendar for reading through the Word of God in a year (Dundee, 30 December 1842), as printed in Memoir and Remains (1892), pp. 618–628

plans.title: Chronological
plans.source: Wellspring’s arrangement (2026). Placements follow the text’s own headings where it has them — a psalm’s superscription, a prophet’s named kings, Ezra 5:1 — and are listed where it does not.

plans.title: Order written
plans.source: “Dating the Bible”, Wikipedia (Tables I, II and IV), which tables the dates most widely held in critical scholarship, citing Brown, Coogan, Collins, Carr, Day, Nelson and others

plans.title: The Septuagint’s order
plans.source: The order of Rahlfs’s Septuaginta, as printed in A New English Translation of the Septuagint (NETS, 2007), contents

plans.title: The 1611 order
plans.source: The Holy Bible (Robert Barker, 1611), contents table “The Bookes called Apocrypha”
